hints: For n = 27 values, the median position is (27 + 1) / 2 = 14th value.
Find the 14th value for Company A from the stem-and-leaf diagram: median = 2710.
The lower quartile is the 7th value (2610), and the upper quartile is the 21st value (2840).
walkthrough:
Determine the position of the median for $n = 27$ employees:
$$\text{Position of median } Q_2 = \frac{27 + 1}{2} = 14\text{th value}$$
$$\text{Median} = 2710$$

Determine the positions and values of the quartiles:
$$\text{Position of } Q_1 = \frac{27 + 1}{4} = 7\text{th value} = 2610$$
$$\text{Position of } Q_3 = 3 \times 7 = 21\text{st value} = 2840$$

Compute the interquartile range:
$$\operatorname{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 2840 - 2610 = 230$$
teacher_walkthrough: Step 1: Count the total number of observations for Company A: $n = 27$.

Step 2: Find the rank of the median:
$$\text{Rank} = \frac{n + 1}{2} = \frac{27 + 1}{2} = 14$$
Reading the 14th value from lowest to highest in the Company A leaves gives:
$$\text{Median} = 2710$$

Step 3: Find the ranks of the lower and upper quartiles:
$$\text{Rank of } Q_1 = \frac{n + 1}{4} = \frac{28}{4} = 7$$
Reading the 7th value gives $Q_1 = 2610$.
$$\text{Rank of } Q_3 = \frac{3(n + 1)}{4} = \frac{3 \times 28}{4} = 21$$
Reading the 21st value gives $Q_3 = 2840$.

Step 4: Calculate the interquartile range:
$$\operatorname{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 2840 - 2610 = 230$$

hints: Consider the presence of extreme values or outliers in either distribution.
Look at Company B: the maximum salary 3090 is an extreme value compared to the rest of the company data.
State that the mean would not be more appropriate because it is distorted by this extreme value; the median is more resistant.
walkthrough:
Assess the suitability of the mean versus the median:
$$\text{No, the mean would not be more appropriate.}$$

Company B has an extreme value ($3090$), which pulls the mean upward and distorts the measure of central tendency; the median is unaffected by extreme outliers and provides a more representative comparison.
teacher_walkthrough:
Step 1: Examine the properties of the mean and the median in the presence of extreme data values:
- The mean takes into account every numerical value, making it highly sensitive to extreme outliers.
- The median is positional and resistant to extreme values.

Step 2: Inspect the salary data for both companies:
Company B contains an extreme value of $3090$, which lies substantially above the third quartile ($2780$).

Step 3: Conclude clearly:
No, the mean would not be a more appropriate measure because Company B has an extreme value ($3090$) that distorts the mean, making the median the preferred measure of central tendency.
